rows.quantity: Delta p = p_core, absolute pressure, time-averaged tail
rows.configuration: single-phase disc, vacuum outside, R=20 mm, sigma=7.2 N/m, p>=0 Tait
rows.why: best reading over the c0 x dx ladder; still outside the 15 % gate, so the end-to-end jump is not evidence of a correct surface-tension model

rows.quantity: same quantity, worst reading of the ladder (shows the spread)
rows.configuration: single-phase disc, vacuum outside, R=20 mm, sigma=7.2 N/m
rows.why: spread over c0 = 5..20 and dx = 1.5..2 mm is 4.1 pts, i.e. the residual is not an EOS noise floor that tuning can remove

rows.quantity: Delta p = p_center - p_interface_band (legacy band differencing)
rows.configuration: single-phase disc, R=20 mm, sigma=7.2 N/m, dx=2 mm, c0=20, 600 relax steps
rows.why: the interface band sits inside the free-surface density deficit (-6..-34 %), so this mouth reports a pressure difference that the fluid does not carry; see laplace_mouth_correction

rows.quantity: percentage points of |error| removed by switching from band differencing to absolute + time-averaged pressure
rows.configuration: uncalibrated control run, dx=2 mm, c0=20 (same disc, same scheme as the row above)
rows.why: same control run (dx=2 mm, c0=20, 1283 steps): the only change is the measurement mouth, so the drop is attributable to the mouth alone

rows.configuration: single-phase disc, R=20 mm, sigma=7.2 N/m, dx=1.5 mm, consistent CSF + fit_quadratic curvature
rows.why: the volume-force integral is the part that the CSF refactor fixed; it is inside the gate at every resolution in the artifact

rows.configuration: single-phase disc, R=20 mm, dx=1.5 mm, fit_quadratic curvature
rows.why: the physically weighted curvature (weight = interface measure) is the quantity that enters the CSF force; it is inside the 3 % band used by the plateau/convergence claims

rows.configuration: single-phase disc, R=20 mm, dx=1.5 mm, fit_quadratic curvature
rows.why: per-particle curvature scatter on the band is large and biased; the claim only holds after delta_s weighting, which is exactly why the force integral (REAL) is the right instrument and the raw band mean is not

rows.quantity: radial line integral of the CSF volume force vs sigma/R (density-matched two-phase)
rows.configuration: two-phase, equal density, sharp colour step + Shepard smoothing, R=100 mm, sigma=0.072 N/m, dx=5 mm
rows.why: with no density jump and no vacuum the pressure closure is not exercised, so this row validates the force operator, not the free-surface pressure closure

rows.configuration: single-phase disc, R=20 mm, dx=1.5 mm, consistent CSF
rows.why: the colour field carries only ~0.74 of the unit surface delta; it is compensated inside the force normalisation but it is the reason absolute force magnitudes must not be read off N_delta directly

rows.quantity: max |v| / sqrt(sigma / (rho R)) against the Adami 2012 bound 0.1
rows.configuration: single-phase disc, R=20 mm, dx=2 mm, c0=20, relaxed 600 steps
rows.why: parasitic current is the second necessary condition for a usable surface-tension model; it passes with margin at every resolution in the artifact
